lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 121, for issue 117, which runs CI's verify tests two at a time.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one twenty-one, for issue one seventeen, which runs C I's verify tests two at a time.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
First, the runner lists the tests: the smoke test, then each verify script. Misnamed scripts are recorded, not run.
It keeps up to two tests running, and checks each one against the budget before it starts.
Each test still runs alone, with its own virtual screen, D-Bus session and home folder.
As each test ends, the results file is rewritten in the same order a serial run would give.
Locally, the build-verify agent now starts the suite in the background, with a 35-minute timeout.
lines.say: Locally, the build verify agent now starts the suite in the background, with a thirty-five minute timeout.

lines.caption: It waits for the completion notice, then reports each test's result and the exit code.
lines.say: It waits for the completion notice, then reports each test's result and the exit code.

lines.caption: On PR 116 the tests took about 13 minutes one after another, and a local run was cut off at 10.
lines.say: On pull request one sixteen the tests took about thirteen minutes one after another, and a local run was cut off at ten.

lines.caption: The key fact: each test already had its own sandbox, so only the runner needed a pool.
Step 1: the smoke test comes first, then the scripts in name order.
Step 2: the budget of 1500 seconds now counts real time since the run began.
lines.say: Step 2: the budget of fifteen hundred seconds now counts real time since the run began.

lines.caption: Step 3: each test writes its result to its own file, and its process id to another.
Step 4: the results come out in serial order, so the shot numbers don't change.
Step 5: the agent's background run also serves the visual-verify skill's capture.
lines.say: Step 5: the agent's background run also serves the visual verify skill's capture.

lines.caption: Step 6: it never waits with a foreground sleep, which the Bash tool would cut off.
Tests finish in any order, but the results keep the serial order.
If the run is stopped, an exit trap kills every running test and keeps the finished results.
JOBS sets how many run at once. Setting it to 1 runs them one at a time, as before.
lines.say: Jobs sets how many run at once. Setting it to one runs them one at a time, as before.

lines.caption: It changes the runner, the verify comment script, the build-verify agent, the visual-verify skill and CLAUDE.md, plus this explainer.
lines.say: It changes the runner, the verify comment script, the build verify agent, the visual verify skill and CLAUDE.md, plus this explainer.

lines.caption: To undo it, run one test at a time again, or revert the PR.
Part 2. How it was built and verified: mock tests, a full run in a cloud container, then CI's runs and shot audits.
lines.say: Part 2. How it was built and verified: mock tests, a full run in a cloud container, then C I's runs and shot audits.

lines.caption: The time to beat is PR 116's serial run: about 13 minutes on CI.
lines.say: The time to beat is pull request one sixteen's serial run: about thirteen minutes on C I.

lines.caption: The new runner keeps the old one's result order and budget rule.
A mock run with stubbed tests kept the serial order, and skipped a test that could overrun the budget.
Stopped partway, it exited 143 and left no test running. A JOBS of zero was refused.
lines.say: Stopped partway, it exited one forty-three and left no test running. A jobs of zero was refused.

lines.caption: In a cloud container, all 20 tests passed in 333 seconds, before the CI review fixes.
lines.say: In a cloud container, all twenty tests passed in three hundred thirty-three seconds, before the C I review fixes.

lines.caption: That run was under 10 minutes, so a longer local run wasn't shown.
lines.say: That run was under ten minutes, so a longer local run wasn't shown.

lines.caption: No Thunar screenshots: the PR changes only CI and agent files.
On CI, after the second review's fixes, all 20 tests passed three at a time.
lines.say: On C I, after the second review's fixes, all twenty tests passed three at a time.

lines.caption: The test step took 5 minutes 55 seconds, against about 13 minutes one at a time on PR 116.
lines.say: The test step took five minutes fifty-five seconds, against about thirteen minutes one at a time on pull request one sixteen.

lines.caption: With three workers, the longest test took 102 seconds, under its 120-second limit, and none timed out.
lines.say: With three workers, the longest test took a hundred and two seconds, under its hundred and twenty second limit, and none timed out.

lines.caption: An independent auditor read all 187 shots from the 20 tests: every one OK, verdict pass.
lines.say: An independent auditor read all hundred and eighty-seven shots from the twenty tests: every one OK, verdict pass.

lines.caption: On the head, with two workers, all 20 tests passed on CI.
lines.say: On the head, with two workers, all twenty tests passed on C I.

lines.caption: The test step took 8 minutes 41 seconds, against 5 minutes 55 seconds with three workers and about 13 serially.
lines.say: The test step took eight minutes forty-one seconds, against five minutes fifty-five seconds with three workers and about thirteen one at a time.

lines.caption: The longest test took 103 seconds, and none timed out.
lines.say: The longest test took a hundred and three seconds, and none timed out.

lines.caption: The auditor read all 187 shots again on the head: every one OK, verdict pass.
lines.say: The auditor read all hundred and eighty-seven shots again on the head: every one OK, verdict pass.

lines.caption: The container and PR 116 times come from different machines; CI's runs on this PR compare them fairly.
lines.say: The container and pull request one sixteen times come from different machines; C I's runs on this pull request compare them fairly.

lines.caption: A local review before the first push found five issues and fixed three.
S1: nothing stopped running tests if the run was killed. The exit trap fixes that.
lines.say: S one: nothing stopped running tests if the run was killed. The exit trap fixes that.

lines.caption: S2: three workers on four processors might make the tests flaky. CI's runs showed none, and the owner chose two.
lines.say: S two: three workers on four processors might make the tests flaky. C I's runs showed none, and the owner chose two.

lines.caption: CI's review found ten findings; all but R6 were fixed at once, and R6 later.
lines.say: C I's review found ten findings; all but R six were fixed at once, and R six later.

lines.caption: Results are kept as each test ends, and the exit trap stops every test cleanly.
The agent's run sets its log folder and waits with a timeout, and JOBS must be a positive number.
lines.say: The agent's run sets its log folder and waits with a timeout, and jobs must be a positive number.

lines.caption: On R6, the load worry, the owner chose two tests at a time.
lines.say: On R six, the load worry, the owner chose two tests at a time.

lines.caption: CI's second review found eight more. R11 kept tests that ended just as the run was stopped.
lines.say: C I's second review found eight more. R eleven kept tests that ended just as the run was stopped.

lines.caption: The rest were fixed too, except R17, a tiny race that was already there, which counts as accepted.
lines.say: The rest were fixed too, except R seventeen, a tiny race that was already there, which counts as accepted.

lines.caption: The third review found eight low ones. R19, an empty log block, now says the test did not start.
lines.say: The third review found eight low ones. R nineteen, an empty log block, now says the test did not start.

lines.caption: The other seven weren't confirmed, and each was accepted with a reason.
CI's next three reviews found twelve low ones. One fix tells a test with no log from one with an empty log.
lines.say: C I's next three reviews found twelve low ones. One fix tells a test with no log from one with an empty log.

lines.caption: Another reads only a log's last 30 lines, and drops trailing blank lines.
lines.say: Another reads only a log's last thirty lines, and drops trailing blank lines.

lines.caption: The last five weren't confirmed, and each was accepted with a reason.
The No log and empty log lines show only when a test has no log or an empty one, which hasn't happened yet.
A local run longer than 10 minutes waits for the suite to grow.
lines.say: A local run longer than ten minutes waits for the suite to grow.

lines.caption: Links to the PR, the issue and the serial reference are at the end of Part 2.
CI's two runs, three and then two at a time, are linked there too.
lines.say: C I's two runs, three and then two at a time, are linked there too.

lines.caption: Part 3. What comes later: no open issue depends on 117, and the PR is ready to merge once CI passes.
lines.say: Part 3. What comes later: no open issue depends on one seventeen, and the PR is ready to merge once C I passes.

lines.caption: This PR runs the tests two at a time.
Next is the merge: you chose two at a time for R6.
lines.say: Next is the merge: you chose two at a time for R six.

lines.caption: After that, each new feature script costs the budget less.
CI ran all 20 tests in 8 minutes 41 seconds, so the PR merges once CI passes on its head.
lines.say: C I ran all twenty tests in eight minutes forty-one seconds, so the pull request merges once C I passes on its head.

lines.caption: With two at a time, each new script adds about half its own time to the run.
Running only changed scripts was left out on purpose, so older features stay tested.
In short: PR 121 runs verify two tests at a time, and local runs finish in the background.
lines.say: In short: pull request one twenty-one runs verify two tests at a time, and local runs finish in the background.
